l23-q01.answer: Concept drift: familiar inputs, changed input-to-output relationship
options: Data drift, since the operating conditions have moved away from the training distribution
Concept drift: familiar inputs, changed input-to-output relationship
Prediction drift, since the model's output distribution is what shifts first in this scenario
Label drift, since the ground truth definition has changed while the inputs have not

l23-q02.answer: The input distribution, and the model's own output distribution
options: Nothing meaningful; without labels there is no measurable notion of model quality
The input distribution, and the model's own output distribution
The model's confidence scores, which fall predictably when the inputs move out of domain
Inference latency, which rises when inputs fall outside the regions the model was optimised for

l23-q03.answer: Above 0.25, with 0.1 to 0.25 worth watching and under 0.1 no meaningful shift
options: Above 0.05, since anything measurable indicates the distribution has moved
Above 0.25, with 0.1 to 0.25 worth watching and under 0.1 no meaningful shift
Above 0.5, since PSI is a log-scaled quantity and small values are expected
Above 1.0, which is the point at which the distributions no longer overlap

l23-q04.answer: A guardrail not tied to a named failure mode is not a guardrail
options: Nothing, provided the checks are implemented before release and reviewed
A guardrail not tied to a named failure mode is not a guardrail
Safety checks belong in the monitoring section rather than the design document
It should quantify the residual risk, since an unquantified safety claim cannot be reviewed

l23-q05.answer: Treat retrieved documents and tool outputs as untrusted input
options: A content filter on retrieved documents, removing any text that resembles an instruction
Treat retrieved documents and tool outputs as untrusted input
A stricter system prompt telling the model to ignore instructions found in documents
A human review step for any document ingested into the index

l23-q06.answer: An explicit input-range check before every prediction
options: Calibration checked against held-out truth, so the reported interval widens appropriately
An explicit input-range check before every prediction
Drift monitoring on the input distribution, tied to a retraining trigger
Output validation against a versioned schema, so a malformed prediction fails loudly

l23-q07.answer: It fails the build when a key metric drops below a threshold
options: It runs the test suite against the trained model rather than the code, catching model-level regressions
It fails the build when a key metric drops below a threshold
It gates deployment on manual approval, so a human signs off before any model reaches production
It compares the new model against the previous one and deploys whichever scores higher

l23-q08.answer: Automation bias, and the response belongs in the system design
options: A training problem: operators need clearer instruction on when to override the model
Automation bias, and the response belongs in the system design
A calibration problem: the model was over-confident and should have reported a wider interval
A user-interface problem: the recommendation should be less prominent on the screen

l23-q10.answer: To show what the detector says when nothing has changed, so a positive result elsewhere means something
options: To calibrate the thresholds, since the null case sets the floor for what counts as a shift
To show what the detector says when nothing has changed, so a positive result elsewhere means something
To warm the cache, so the subsequent comparisons run at a comparable speed
To demonstrate that PSI and the KS test disagree even when there is no drift

l23-q11.answer: Because the artifact that was tested is the artifact that ships
options: Because containers are faster to start than a fresh environment, which matters when scaling out inference workers
Because the artifact that was tested is the artifact that ships
Because container registries provide the versioning that git cannot give to model weights
Because most cloud serving platforms accept only containers, so it is a deployment requirement
